title: CLO 2025 Academic Month: The Development of Underwear in the Digital Age
description: CLO 2025 Official Academic Monthly Course Review Now Available! Mr. Thomas Lee, Head of the Digital Department at Regine Virginie (Shenzhen) Co., Ltd., will explain in detail from the company's perspective how digitalization drives the apparel industry and improves traditional operational models.
transcript:
Hello everyone, first of all, thank you for the invitation. I am very honored to share some of my 3D experience with you on behalf of my company.

First, I have worked in this industry for more than 20 years. Then, in 2018, I started my 3D journey during my first year of military service. At that time, we often discussed trends in the fashion industry. However, I realized that 3D fashion is the future trend.

In the past 7 years of my 3D fashion experience, I have worked with different fashion brands and companies. According to the customers’ various needs, we provide different 3D outputs. For example, when working with some brands, we usually provide 3D CPOJ files to the customers. Then, the customers follow our requirements to review our products.

For example, for customers who do not yet have 3D software, we provide front and back views and some images to showcase the fashion. Through different pictures, including virtual images and images showing various pressure marks, we present the fashion results and cooperate with them. Additionally, we can create different fashion accessories, which I will share with you later.

I will share four different aspects with you. First is customer fashion.

Next page.

Generally, in our industry, regardless of the project or product, fashion can be divided into the stages of product development and production. According to these stages, we can apply 3D technology.

For example, in traditional fashion, we may start from scratch based on customer requirements, fabric support, and style. Then, we slowly produce the fabric, cut, assemble, and conduct fitting tests. This process may take about 14 working days but may not necessarily yield good results. Sometimes after seeing the sample, it is wasted.

This process takes 14 working days. However, using 3D technology, we can shorten this to about 7 days or even faster. We can apply it to our fast-moving board and produce a virtual sample simultaneously. This not only improves sales but also provides a seamless connection for customers.

In 3D, we can select and modify models. Besides saving costs, we also save time. As I mentioned, we can use different 3D samples, such as pressure maps and transparency maps, to visualize results. Then, we can directly share models with customers on a platform for sample inspection before proceeding to the next step.

In the past, we continuously worked on samples before going to market. Now, with the 3D process, we can directly display 3D samples, inspect them, produce possibly one or two physical samples, and then launch to market.

Next page.

Regarding sample types, we can divide them into two categories. First, we use sample types to display different samples. Generally, in the sample section, there are two types: the first is design samples. Each sample cycle takes 14 days, plus 7 days for customer review, totaling about 21 days. Sometimes, a second round is necessary. After the second round, the sample is taken to the sales section.

After the sales section, customers may request samples for checking and testing. Before mass production, there is a mass production sample section. So, there are different sample types.

However, in 3D, we can reduce many unnecessary physical samples. For example, we can apply 3D to sales boards and magnetic boards. We can build boards in 3D and use virtual SMS (Sample Management System) to apply them to SMS, checking for any issues such as defects in different telemachines and compliance with regulations.

On the right side, you can see some products from our company. All are built this way. Whether underwear or sports underwear, we can place them on different boards, allowing customers to apply our 3D products at different stages.

For example, mid-season traditionally takes about 168 days to build different boards and produce them. Using 3D, this can be reduced to approximately 90 days.

That’s all. Thank you.

Next slide, please.

02 is the digital production network we discussed. As I said, we have different stages through 3D. Using our 3D tools, we can apply different 3D needs in various scenarios.

For example, we can roughly divide what we call normal 3D. In this 3D model, there are multiple modeling capabilities. We can apply products you have developed. They can be integrated into 3D so that when the product passes to our 3D editor, the 3D laptop uses the 3D training system with the 3D machine or can respond through the purchase and acceptance system.

The public can convert the product into 3D and allow pattern comparison. I will move on to other results that I find very exciting.

This platform allows the product to be passed through various sales environments, such as shops, virtual showrooms, animation, and other scenarios.

Next page.

This is an example. You can see about 10 styles. Initially, we had only one style. From this one style, we can create 10 different styles by adding different fabrics and transparency styles. From these 10 styles, we can create over 100 styles by adding variations.

Thus, in 3D printing, this greatly improves efficiency.

Next page.

As I said, starting from one style, we can add different prints and effects and change a simple style into a more sporty one. These are styles some of our customers have used before. From a simple style, we can add fabric, print, and logos to create different styles.

Next page.

In general, besides the closet platform where we can view styles, we can add front and back views to show customers the styles. We can also provide selection maps for customers to quickly see style effects.

We can also offer transparency and pressure maps to help understand which styles need changes.

Thank you.

Next page.

Here are all the necessary color versions. In the closet platform, we have simple colorways and can add different colorways, replacing some traditional ones.

There are different versions: first, wasting time; second, wasting unnecessary materials; and third, faster customer display.

Next pages.  
[Several slides with no additional text.]

Then, you can access the Cloud Closet platform, which serves as a database. We share our 3D data with customers through this database. Customers follow their different requirements.

Generally, customers provide VQS (Virtual Quality Standards), which are requirements for virtual quality. We improve communication methods according to these requirements and quickly approve payments.

As I said, we only have normal 3D. Why do we call these 3D sales? Because beyond the usual 3D, we can add different 3D effects. For example, we can place more realistic 3D brochures on the cloud platform.

According to various requirements, we can place these documents on a timeline and set them on tables for photos.

Next page.

We can add more AI features beyond the 3D design I mentioned. We can add internal structure images and more visuals, even create animations. From animations, we can show product features such as breathability.

Of course, these things cannot be achieved with just one source.

Next page.

Besides structural images, we can create display images. For example, starting from a virtual platform for a person, we can create a model and rotate it to display different colors.

There are other features such as virtual showrooms. Let me give an example: traditionally, we finished producing a product set and placed it in a scene for photos, which took two to three months.

Using this 3D model (the one on the right as an example), we can finish in about two to three weeks. Some customers can directly choose a product here; we can add AR products, allowing quick selection and ordering.

Will it be successful? Yes, I believe it will.

There are many other examples where you can place a product and view it instantly.

Personally, I think this is one of the most important points to analyze what we are doing now.

The first point is that we sometimes don’t know what to do. There are many ways to analyze this, so continuous analysis is necessary.

The first point is to consider the material in detail.

The second point is that if you have a 3D model, you can do a scan. In fabric, we can roughly divide texture and fabric properties. Through some products, we can more accurately obtain the texture and properties needed.

Before concluding, we must understand that different countries have different fitting patterns and requirements. For example, on the right side of the picture, we see a larger and a thinner model, which is easy to understand.

We can use different requirements to produce different fabrics for different customers, which results in significant differences.

Besides 3D, a major issue is applying fabric in 3D. For example, we have a pattern, place it, and use fabric to create the pattern. Then, we can modify it to make it easier for customers to view.

On the right side, if fabric use is unknown, stitching may be needed, resulting in visible stitches. We must understand fabric requirements well to apply fabric in 3D and achieve better results.

Next slide, please.

Besides what I mentioned, the final point is that for a 3D designer, personal involvement and coordination skills are very important.

We can apply 3D to many things. For example, the image on the left shows seamless design. Besides sewing products, we can apply 3D to seamless and integrated styles.

On the right, we see how to apply 3D to different lower-body styles.

We can apply 3D to our 3D app, sales points, and virtual events, covering many aspects.

Let me conclude.

In the clothing industry, traditionally, production scales were large. Now, we have smaller units. Many older brand items are now produced more flexibly.

In the industry, we have reduced costs, enabled quick replacements, and met demands.

Through the industry’s current requirements—production units, sales, efficiency, and production costs—we can meet the demand for digital products.

This school can produce new talents and is a good place for cooperation.

We hope the school can collaborate with us to create a cross-digital integrated ecosystem, enabling students to connect with our production line.

Finally, I want to say a few points: we need to shorten the gap between integration and the industry so that our future students can graduate and quickly compete in the industry.

They can rapidly apply digitalization, innovate, and be trained in 3D design and real-time 3D layout.

We can also teach them how to do 3D sales, improving future opportunities.

Thank you, everyone.

As you can see, this is a relatively simple T-tie bracelet. We can add different effects to show you on foreign TV. We can also show variations for different body types, not just one person.

Thank you.

chunks.content: # The Development of Underwear in the Digital Age ## Introduction to 3D Fashion Technology in Underwear Development This section outlines the speaker's 20+ years of industry experience and the rise of 3D fashion technology since 2018, emphasizing its transformative impact on underwear design and production processes. The speaker began exploring 3D fashion technology during military service in 2018 and has since collaborated with various fashion brands, tailoring 3D outputs to customer needs. Typical deliverables include 3D CPOJ files for clients with 3D software and front/back images or pressure maps for those without. This flexibility facilitates visualization of fashion results and accessory design. ## 3D Technology in Product Development and Production Stages This section explains how 3D technology accelerates the traditional fashion product development cycle, reduces costs, and improves sample accuracy through virtual prototyping and visualization tools like pressure and transparency maps. Traditional underwear sample development involves fabric sourcing, cutting, assembly, and fitting tests, typically taking 14 working days, often resulting in wasted samples. Using 3D technology, this timeframe can be halved to approximately 7 days by concurrently producing virtual samples on fast-moving boards. This approach facilitates model selection and modification, enables seamless customer collaboration through shared platforms, and drastically reduces physical sample iterations. ## Sample Types and 3D Integration in Production This part details various sample categories—design samples, sales samples, and mass production samples—and how 3D technology minimizes physical sample requirements by integrating virtual samples into Sample Management Systems (SMS) and compliance checks. Design sample cycles usually span 14 days, with an additional 7 days for customer review, totaling about 21 days. Sometimes, further iterations are necessary before samples proceed to sales and mass production stages. The 3D process enables creation of virtual sales boards and magnetic boards, allowing sample evaluation through SMS and telemachine inspections. For instance, mid-season board production traditionally takes 168 days but can be reduced to 90 days using 3D. ## Digital Production Network and 3D Modeling Capabilities This section covers the digital production network enabled by 3D tools, including integration with 3D editors, pattern comparison, and connection to purchase and acceptance systems. Normal 3D models incorporate multiple modeling capabilities and can integrate existing product designs. Products can be converted into 3D formats for pattern comparison and passed through various sales environments such as virtual showrooms, animation, and retail scenarios, enhancing product presentation and decision-making. ## Style Variations and Efficiency Improvements through 3D This section emphasizes how a single base style can be transformed into numerous variations by applying different fabrics, transparency effects, prints, and logos, significantly enhancing design efficiency. Starting from one underwear style, designers can generate 10 different styles by adding fabrics and transparency, and over 100 styles by further adding variations. This scalability accelerates design iteration and diversification, supporting rapid product development. ## Visualization Tools: Front/Back Views, Pressure, and Transparency Maps This section describes visualization tools provided to customers, such as front/back views and selection maps, and how pressure and transparency maps assist in identifying design modifications.

chunks.content: ## Style Variations and Efficiency Improvements through 3D This section emphasizes how a single base style can be transformed into numerous variations by applying different fabrics, transparency effects, prints, and logos, significantly enhancing design efficiency. Starting from one underwear style, designers can generate 10 different styles by adding fabrics and transparency, and over 100 styles by further adding variations. This scalability accelerates design iteration and diversification, supporting rapid product development. ## Visualization Tools: Front/Back Views, Pressure, and Transparency Maps This section describes visualization tools provided to customers, such as front/back views and selection maps, and how pressure and transparency maps assist in identifying design modifications. The closet platform offers multiple colorways and quick style previews, facilitating faster customer decisions. Pressure and transparency maps provide detailed feedback on style fit and fabric behavior, enabling targeted improvements before production. ## Cloud Closet Platform and Virtual Quality Standards (VQS) This section explains the Cloud Closet platform as a centralized 3D data repository shared with customers, supporting compliance with Virtual Quality Standards and streamlining communication and payment approval. Customers submit VQS requirements that define virtual quality benchmarks. The platform accommodates these standards by organizing 3D sales brochures, timelines, and photo tables, enhancing the virtual product presentation and approval workflow. ## Advanced 3D Features: AI, Animations, and Virtual Showrooms This section explores AI-enhanced 3D design elements, including internal structure visualizations, animations demonstrating features like breathability, and virtual showrooms that reduce physical photo shoot times from months to weeks. Animations showcase functional product characteristics such as breathability. Virtual showrooms enable customers to rotate models, view multiple colors, and select products quickly, including AR-enabled ordering. These tools offer significant time savings and enhanced customer engagement. ## Material Analysis and Fabric Application in 3D This section discusses detailed material analysis, 3D scanning of fabric textures and properties, and the importance of accurately applying fabric in 3D models to avoid issues like visible stitching. Different countries’ fitting patterns and fabric requirements must be considered. 3D models use scanned data to replicate fabric texture and behavior precisely. Proper fabric placement and stitching simulation in 3D are critical for realistic visualization and customer approval. ## Seamless Design and 3D Applications Across Product Types This section highlights the application of 3D technology beyond traditional sewing to seamless underwear designs and diverse lower-body styles, expanding the scope of 3D usage in product development, sales, and virtual events. 3D design supports seamless and integrated styles without sewing. It is also used in 3D apps, retail sales points, and virtual events, facilitating a broad range of applications across the underwear product lifecycle. ## Industry Trends: Flexible Production and Digital Integration This section summarizes industry shifts toward smaller-scale, flexible production units enabled by digital technology, reducing costs, speeding replacements, and meeting evolving market demands. Traditional large-scale production is giving way to more agile manufacturing, supported by digital workflows. This transition improves efficiency, cost control, and responsiveness to consumer needs.

chunks.content: It is also used in 3D apps, retail sales points, and virtual events, facilitating a broad range of applications across the underwear product lifecycle. ## Industry Trends: Flexible Production and Digital Integration This section summarizes industry shifts toward smaller-scale, flexible production units enabled by digital technology, reducing costs, speeding replacements, and meeting evolving market demands. Traditional large-scale production is giving way to more agile manufacturing, supported by digital workflows. This transition improves efficiency, cost control, and responsiveness to consumer needs. ## Education and Future Talent Development in 3D Fashion This final section stresses the importance of bridging the gap between academia and industry by training students in 3D design, real-time layout, and 3D sales to prepare them for competitive digital fashion careers. Collaboration between educational institutions and industry partners can create integrated digital ecosystems, enabling students to engage directly with production lines. Emphasis is placed on rapid digital adoption, innovation, and skills development to meet future workforce needs. --- # Summary of Key Technologies and Concepts - **3D CPOJ files:** Industry-standard 3D file format for fashion samples. - **Pressure and Transparency Maps:** Visualization tools to assess fit and fabric behavior. - **Sample Management System (SMS):** Digital platform integrating virtual samples and compliance checks. - **Cloud Closet Platform:** Centralized 3D data repository facilitating quality control and sales. - **Virtual Quality Standards (VQS):** Customer-defined benchmarks for virtual product quality. - **AI and Animations:** Enhance 3D presentations with internal structure visuals and functional demos. - **Virtual Showrooms and AR:** Interactive environments for product visualization and ordering. - **3D Scanning:** Captures fabric texture and properties for realistic 3D application. - **Seamless Design:** 3D technology applied to integrated, no-sew underwear styles. --- This document encapsulates the detailed processes, technologies, and industry implications of 3D fashion development specifically applied to underwear in the digital age.
